title: Wrong with Confidence: Measuring Hallucination, Overconfidence and Identity-Conditioned Behaviour in Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.18728v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models answer underspecified questions readily, and accuracy-only evaluation rewards guessing over abstaining. Observational studies link query underspecification to hallucination, but they cannot separate the effect of missing information from item difficulty, and they rarely ask what the model tells the user. We report a pre-registered, paired behavioural study of five open-weight models (Gemma 3 27B, Gemma 4 31B, gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B and Nemotron 3 Super). Each of 142 factual questions was posed in a fully specified form and in a referentially underspecified form with the same answer key, and three probes measured identity-conditioned behaviour. Two raters scored 5,620 responses under a fixed rubric; effects were estimated with mixed-effects models. Without the referent, the models sought clarification on 33.7% of prompts and answered the rest. Among attempted answers, the error rate rose from 39.1% to 52.

translated_title: 自信地犯错：测量大语言模型中的幻觉、过度自信与身份条件化行为
translated_abstract: 大语言模型会轻易回答欠明确的问题，而仅以准确率为标准的评估奖励猜测而非弃答。观察性研究将查询欠明确与幻觉联系起来，但它们无法将信息缺失的影响与题目本身的难度区分开来，也很少关注模型究竟告诉了用户什么。我们报告了一项预先注册的配对行为研究，涉及五个开放权重模型（Gemma 3 27B、Gemma 4 31B、gpt-oss-120b、Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B 和 Nemotron 3 Super）。142 个事实性问题分别以完全明确的形式和具有相同答案标准的指代欠明确形式提出，并使用三个探针测量身份条件化行为。两名评分员按照固定评分标准对 5,620 个回答进行了评分；效应通过混合效应模型进行估计。在缺少指代对象的情况下，模型仅在 33.7% 的提示中寻求澄清，而对其余问题直接作答。在尝试回答的问题中，错误率从 39.1% 上升到 52……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究通过预先注册的配对行为实验发现，面对缺少指代信息的欠明确问题时，大语言模型大多不寻求澄清而直接作答，且错误率显著上升，揭示了模型在信息缺失情境下以自信姿态产生幻觉的系统性过度自信行为。
en_tdlr: This pre-registered paired behavioural study reveals that large language models rarely seek clarification when facing referentially underspecified questions, instead answering directly with significantly elevated error rates, systematically quantifying overconfident hallucination and identity-conditioned behaviour across five open-weight models.
